audits.published_statement: The tree quotes no published statement. The usual datum, not read here: nuclear saturation density n0 ~ 0.16 fm^-3, mass density ~2.7e17 kg/m^3, energy per nucleon ~ -16 MeV. Symmetric matter has zero pressure at saturation. What the tree says: seatindex.py:95-96 'at l ~ 100 km it is BELOW nuclear density. Matter that seats a conjugate point exists in nature; it is called a neutron star.'; :370 'vs nuclear ~1e35 Pa'; :374-375 chk(tkk_required(1.0e5) < 1.0e35); :405-406 'below nuclear density beyond about 100 km'.
published_hypotheses: (datum, not read) n0 is the density at which symmetric matter's energy per nucleon is lowest. Its energy density is eps0 = n0 (m_N c^2 + E/A) and its pressure there is zero, so the right 'nuclear' figure to compare with T_kk is an energy density, not a pressure.
(physics the tree uses) For a perfect fluid, T_kk = (eps + p)(k.u)^2. Comparing T_kk with eps directly needs k.u = -1 and p << eps.

(physics the tree uses) The Sturm threshold applies to a stretch of length l. 'Below nuclear density' compares density only. It does not ask whether a region at that density and of length l can exist.
hypothesis_drift: UNIT WORDING (a discrepancy, not a refutation), seatindex.py:370. The tree writes '1e35 Pa' and the key says 'pressure', but the meaningful comparison is with the saturation energy density, since the pressure at saturation is about zero. The comparison the tree actually makes is energy density against T_kk, which is the right kind.

VALUE (a computed internal inconsistency), seatindex.py:370,375 against warpdrive.py:148, emwarp.py:225 and drivespec.py:39. 1e35 Pa is 624 MeV/fm^3. That is 4.84x the tree's own 2.3e17 kg/m^3 x c^2 = 2.067e34 Pa, and 4.23x eps0 at n0 = 0.16 (3.98x-4.66x over n0 = 0.145-0.170). 1e35 Pa is about 4 n0, a neutron-star-core figure. The printed margin at 100 km is x10.5; the true margin is about x2.2-2.5.

DROPPED (normalisation), seatindex.py:370-375. T_kk = (eps + p) w^2 with w = -k.u, checked with sympy. The tree sets T_kk equal to eps, which assumes w = 1 and p = 0. Both hold at saturation and the verdict does not move, but the assumption is now named.

DROPPED (geometry), seatindex.py:95-96 ('it is called a neutron star'). A uniform ball of diameter l at the threshold density has 2GM/(Rc^2) = pi^2/6 = 1.645 for every l (sympy, exact, weak-field estimate). That is past the Buchdahl limit of 8/9. A thin rod has G mu/c^2 = pi^2 a^2/(4 l^2) and escapes that bound. So the neutron-star sentence needs the unstated assumption that the seating region is long along the ray, not a compact ball. Recorded here, not repaired.

verifiers.reason:
I copied the script to verify/rederive/ and ran it unchanged. All 14 checks pass (SELFTEST OK, exit 0), and every number the audit quotes comes out the same: T_COEFF = 9.505325e43 Pa m^2, tkk(100 km) = 9.505e33 Pa, eps0(0.16) = 2.366e34 Pa, 1e35/eps0 = 4.23, 1e35/(2.3e17 c^2) = 4.84, break-even n0 = 0.0643 fm^-3, crossover 30.8 km with 1e35 against 61.5-67.8 km otherwise, ball compactness pi^2/6, rod G mu/c^2 = pi^2 a^2/(4 l^2), and a Sturm ratio of 0.209 for the illustrative neutron star. A separate hand calculation with hard-coded constants and no scipy gives the same values (eps0 = 2.3659e34, 4.2267, 0.4018, 63.39 km, 0.2095).

ENCODING. The script compares T_kk with the saturation energy density, the comparison seatindex.py:370-375 actually makes, and it scans n0 rather than relying on one unread value. So the verdict does not depend on anything NAMED-NOT-READ. It checks the claim itself, not a toy version of it. Two parts are toys, and the audit already says so: the ball-compactness check is a weak-field estimate, not a GR solution, and the neutron-star numbers (1.4 Msun, 12 km) are illustrative and were not read.

VACUITY GUARD: seven mutations, each with its target hypothesis negated, and all seven make the selftest fail (exit 1).
- Tree value set to 5e33: the verdict check fails.
- n0 scanned at 0.04-0.063: the eps0 verdict and both crossover checks fail.
- Tree rho set to 1e17: the internal-constant verdict fails.
- l = 31.6 km: the verdict and the break-even checks fail.
- Sign of E/A flipped: the band check fails.
- Wrong perfect-fluid tensor: the T_kk identity fails.
- Wrong ball volume: the compactness check fails.
None of the checks passes vacuously.

Discrepancies I found, none of which moves the grade:
1. Provenance mislabel. The audit and script say 'CODATA 2018 via scipy 1.17.1', but scipy 1.17.1 reports _current_codata = 'CODATA 2022'. The values used (c, G = 6.6743e-11, m_n = 939.56542194 MeV, m_p = 938.27208943 MeV) agree to every digit the result needs, so this is a wording correction only.
2. The audit's bounds of 3.9-4.7 and 60-70 km were set after one check failed and was widened. They describe the scan; they do not test anything independently.
3. The tree's own 2.3e17 kg/m^3 corresponds to n0 = 0.137 fm^-3, below the scanned band of 0.145-0.170. The audit handles it as a separate comparison, which is right. It is still well above the break-even of 0.064.
4. The illustrative neutron star sits about 5x below the Sturm threshold along its own diameter (ratio 0.209). If anything, this strengthens the audit's point that the sentence 'it is called a neutron star' rests on an unstated assumption about the shape of the region. audits.name: Null and dominant energy conditions for a thin-shell surface stress (NEC: sigma + p >= 0; DEC: sigma >= 0 and sigma >= |p|)

source.located: Definition: Hawking & Ellis, The Large Scale Structure of Space-Time (CUP 1973) sec. 4.3. It predates arXiv and is NAMED-NOT-READ. It was read in two restatements. (i) The principal-pressure (type-I) forms are in F.S.N. Lobo, 'Exotic solutions in General Relativity: traversable wormholes and warp drive spacetimes', arXiv:0710.4474v1 (2007), sec. II.F.1, eqs (62)-(70): NEC 'for all i, rho + p_i >= 0' (64); WEC 'rho >= 0 and for all i, rho + p_i >= 0' (66); DEC 'rho >= 0 and for all i, p_i in [-rho, +rho]' (70). (ii) The thin-shell forms themselves, in exactly the tree's notation, are in C. Choi & R.E. Grady, 'Sharp Tangential NEC Minimization and Israel Surface Layers in Schwarzschild Mass Interpolations', arXiv:2608.09963v1 (26 Jul 2026), Remark 7.6: 'For a surface stress tensor S^A_B = diag(-sigma, p, p) the shell null, weak, and dominant conditions read sigma + p >= 0; sigma >= 0 and sigma + p >= 0; and sigma >= 0 and |p| <= sigma.' The Lanczos/Israel sigma and p that the conditions are applied to were audited by the sibling israel-lanczos-poisson-visser-thin-shell.json. They are not re-read here; they are re-derived in sympy.
source.via: Every alphaXiv call made this pass returned 'alphaXiv assistant quota exceeded': answer_pdf_queries on 1112.2057 and gr-qc/0410087, get_paper_content on 1112.2057, and discover_papers. The texts actually read are alphaXiv full-text extractions that earlier stages of this workflow banked in the scratchpad, each read this pass at the lines given: d67/src/casmag/all/0710.4474v1.txt lines 1826-1936; 2608.09963v1.txt lines 1-20 and 2626-2660; 2103.11698v2.txt lines 1457-1466; gr-qc_0301003v2.txt lines 611-617; 0901.1153v3.txt lines 2148-2175. Hawking-Ellis 1973 and Visser 1995 were not read.

audits.published_statement: Type-I forms (Lobo 2007, restating Hawking-Ellis via Visser), for T^{mu nu} = diag(rho, p_1, p_2, p_3). NEC: for all i, rho + p_i >= 0 (eq 64). WEC: rho >= 0 and for all i, rho + p_i >= 0 (eq 66). DEC: T_{mu nu}U^mu U^nu >= 0 and T^{mu nu}U_nu not spacelike (eq 69), i.e. rho >= 0 and for all i, p_i in [-rho, +rho] (eq 70). Thin-shell forms (Choi-Grady 2026, Remark 7.6): for S^A_B = diag(-sigma, p, p), 'the shell null, weak, and dominant conditions read sigma + p >= 0; sigma >= 0 and sigma + p >= 0; and sigma >= 0 and |p| <= sigma.' The same paper's title and sec. 2 call sigma + p (rho + p_t in the bulk) the TANGENTIAL NEC.
published_hypotheses: Pointwise classical conditions on a stress-energy tensor (Lobo 2007 sec. II.F.1: classical matter is believed to obey them; certain quantum fields violate them).
A type-I (diagonalisable) stress tensor with principal pressures p_i (Lobo eq 62).

Thin-shell forms: a 2+1 surface stress S^A_B = diag(-sigma, p, p) with isotropic tangential pressure, the conditions evaluated on the shell world-volume with the induced metric (Choi-Grady Remark 7.6, the 'shell' conditions).
The conditions are evaluated on the given (here static) sigma and p. The definitions assert nothing about perturbed configurations.
hypothesis_drift: NEC SCOPE IS NOT NAMED (stability.py:150-151 nec_holds; the printed NEC column at stability.py:228-232 and in report() at 291-298). The tree's 'NEC', sigma + p >= 0, is exactly the published SHELL (tangential, 2+1) null condition (Choi-Grady Remark 7.6), but the tree drops the shell/tangential qualifier. Now take the 4D distributional tensor T = diag(sigma, 0, p, p) delta(l), whose normal pressure is zero. Lobo's eq (64) requires rho + p_i >= 0 for every i, including the normal direction. So the Hawking-Ellis NEC for that tensor needs sigma >= 0 AND sigma + p >= 0, which is the surface WEC. z3 checks this (D3) and gives a counterexample (D5): sigma = -1, p = 2 passes nec_holds, while the radial null vector (1,1,0,0) gives T_kk = sigma < 0. Consequence for the tree: none. sigma > 0 for every m/R > 0 (z3, B), nothing rests on nec_holds alone, and the surface DEC implies the 4D NEC (z3).
DEC: NO DRIFT. dec_holds at stability.py:145-147 is Choi-Grady's shell DEC, and it is Lobo eq (70) with the tangential p_i. z3 (D1) shows it is also EXACTLY the 4D DEC of the distributional tensor.

SCOPE IS UNDERSTATED, NOT OVERSTATED. The tree claims 'at every compactness tested' (stability.py:35-36) and 'measured' (:304-306); the selftest at :238-239 tests only m/R in {0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 2.0}. The rederivation proves sigma > 0, p < 0 and sigma - |p| = sigma + p > 0 for EVERY m/R > 0: sympy identities, plus z3 quantifying over the reals. |p|/sigma = x(2-3x)/8 + O(x^3) and tends to 1/4, so sigma - |p| never falls below (3/4) sigma.

STATIC ONLY: an unnamed scope, with no consequence for the statement as used. The conditions are checked at the static Lanczos sigma_0 and p_0 (stability.py:132-143). The DEC along a perturbed trajectory under the EOS p' = beta^2 sigma' (stability.py:163-173) is neither claimed nor checked.

WORDING (stability.py:11, :24, :226, :304, 'THE SHELL IS ORDINARY MATTER'). The source's conditions are necessary conditions on a stress tensor. They do not certify that a matter model with sigma > 0 and a tension |p| <= sigma exists. The source supports the tree's word as 'energy-condition-satisfying' and no further. This is a discrepancy of wording, not a refutation.
CANONICAL CITATION: the canonical entry's 'stability.py:238-239' is the selftest check 'DOMINANT energy condition holds throughout'. The verdict prose is at 303-306. Bookkeeping only.

audits.lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not apply to this result. It is a definition: Hawking-Ellis energy conditions specialised to a 2+1 surface stress and applied to closed-form Israel values. No measured quantity enters, so the originators could not have lacked a datum. What the tree's text does not show is the difference between the tangential (surface) NEC and the 4D NEC of the distributional tensor. That is a matter of statement, not data, and it is already in the literature (Lobo 2007 eq 64 with p_n = 0; Choi-Grady 2026 'tangential'). Having it changes nothing here: z3 proves sigma > 0 for every m/R > 0, and that the surface DEC implies the 4D NEC. Evidence the other way: quantum fields are known to violate the pointwise classical conditions (Lobo 2007 II.F.1). The tree applies them to a classical shell and claims nothing quantum, so this is a limit of scope, not an error.
audits.grade_evidence: The verdict rests on the DEC (stability.py:35-36, 145-147, 304-306). The tree's sigma and p are the Lanczos/Israel values: sympy agrees to 1e-14, and the printed columns reproduce to 4 s.f. The claim of the DEC 'at every compactness tested' is proved for EVERY m/R > 0 (sympy identities plus z3). No datum enters. Three findings are recorded and not repaired, and none moves the grade. First, nec_holds is the TANGENTIAL shell NEC without that qualifier; read as a 4D statement it also needs sigma >= 0 (z3 counterexample sigma=-1, p=2). But sigma > 0 on the whole device family, and the DEC implies the 4D NEC. Second, the source supports 'ORDINARY MATTER' only as 'energy-condition-satisfying'. audits.published_statement: Abstract (p.1): 'We study a free, linear, massless scalar field with arbitrary curvature coupling in the context of perturbation theory about the flat spacetime/vacuum solution, and we modify the perturbed semiclassical equations by the "reduction of order" procedure to eliminate spurious solutions. We also restrict attention to the limit in which the lengthscales determined by the state and metric are much larger than the Planck length. At first order in the metric and state perturbations, and for pure states of the scalar field, we find that the ANEC integral vanishes ... For mixed states, the ANEC integral can be negative. However, we prove that if we average the ANEC integral transverse to the geodesic, using a suitable Planck scale smearing function, a strictly positive result is obtained in all cases except for the trivial flat spacetime/vacuum solution. Similar results hold for pure states at second order in perturbation theory, when we additionally specialize to the situation where incoming classical gravitational radiation does not dominate the first order metric perturbation. These results suggest ... that if traversable wormholes do exist as self-consistent solutions of the semiclassical equations, they cannot be macroscopic but must be "Planck scale".' Sec. I C (p.5): 'a one-parameter family (with parameter denoted by eps) of spacetimes (M, g_ab(eps)) and quantum states satisfying Eq. (1.1) [G_ab = 8 pi <T_ab>], with the spacetime reducing to Minkowski spacetime and the quantum state reducing to the vacuum state when eps = 0'; eqs (1.6)-(1.7) expand the state and the metric to O(eps^2) + O(eps^3). Sec. V (p.27): positivity of ANEC 'to order eps^2 ... actually fails ... Nevertheless, we do obtain a positivity result involving a transversely smeared version of the ANEC integral.' FW's OWN statement of semiclassical gravity's domain (p.2): objects that 'always lie outside the domain of validity of the semiclassical theory, either because the curvature scales are Planckian somewhere in the corresponding spacetimes, or because the quantum fluctuations in the stress tensor are comparable to its expected value.' p.4: 'we will be forced to resort to perturbation theory about the trivial solution'. p.5: 'the behavior of solutions in semiclassical gravity -- within the domain of validity of that theory -- may be qualitatively similar to classical solutions.'
published_hypotheses: H1 matter: a single free, linear (non-self-interacting), massless scalar field with arbitrary curvature coupling xi (abstract; p.3; p.5)
H2 self-consistency: G_ab = 8 pi <T_ab> (eq. 1.1), whose only source is the quantum field's <T_ab>, with no classical matter
H3 one-parameter family reducing to Minkowski + vacuum at eps = 0 (p.5); results through O(eps^2), O(eps^3) dropped (eqs 1.6-1.7); no remainder estimate on the pages read
H4 reduction of order applied to the perturbed semiclassical equations (abstract; p.27 eqs 4.20, 4.23)
H5 long wavelengths: lengthscales >> Planck length (alpha >> 1; unknown corrections O((ln alpha)^2/alpha^6) in eq. 4.23)
H6 Hadamard 2-point distributions with positivity; in-data at J^- under 'suitable asymptotic conditions' (p.5)
H7 the second-order pure-state result also needs incoming classical gravitational radiation not to dominate h^(1); <T^(2)[h1,h1]> is not evaluated and approximate eq. (3.59) is used (p.27)
H8 complete achronal null geodesic; the conclusion is TRANSVERSELY SMEARED ANEC (Planck-scale smearing), and unsmeared ANEC fails
H9 globally hyperbolic spacetime (p.3)

The audit graded from pp.1-5, 27 and 50 only. In this stage alphaXiv returned the full text of gr-qc/9602052v2, banked at scratchpad/d67/verify/refute/fw-9602052-fulltext.txt. That made it possible to test the audit's own upgrade route: a passage on the unread pages where FW put O(1) metric deviations outside semiclassical gravity's domain. No such passage exists.

What the full text shows:
- p.8, Sec. II B: an expected metric is meaningful only where fluctuations of the geometry about its mean are negligibly small. This is a fluctuation criterion, not an amplitude one.
- p.9: under the one-loop scheme, corrections are about L_p^2/L^2, 'and consequently the domain of validity of the equation is restricted to L >> L_p'. Under the 1/N scheme the equation holds up to L ~ sqrt(N) L_p.
- p.19, Sec. IV: 'approximate equations, with domain of validity is L >> L_p'.
- Sec. IV B (pp.19-21) says the opposite of what the tree attributes to FW. Semiclassical theory 'should be able to accurately describe ... very large global deviations from classical solutions', and Eq. (2.6) 'may predict large deviations from classical behavior even though L >> L_p everywhere'.
- In the smeared-ANEC discussion, a spacetime 'presumably lies outside the domain of validity' only when its tensors vary over Planck lengths.
- Searches for 'weak field', 'small curvature' and 'beyond perturbation' return nothing.

So FW define the domain by a length scale plus fluctuations, never by metric amplitude, and small eps is a hypothesis of their analysis only. The attribution drift at throatmass.py:68-72 (repeated in the ledger's O5 row) is now confirmed on the full text, not just on the pages the audit read. The tree's other use, the decline at throatmass.py:62-64 and :161, still stands.

The grade also holds against the other direction:
- Not WRONG: nothing in FW is refuted.
- Not STANDS: the upgrade condition is now checked and fails.

- higgs.py vev() and lam() name no scheme. lam() actually defines λ := m_h²/(2v²). That makes 8|V_min| = v² m_h² a definitional identity in code, while its physical use (static response, vacuum depth, cost) is tree-level.
- Tree level is named only at address.py:27-29, and only for the α/v statement.

Why WRONG and DATA-DEPENDENT fail:
- I re-ran the rederive script: exit 0, ALL CHECKS PASS.
- No moved datum shifts a verdict. The largest move is 3.1e-3, from the MS-bar v. Against that, the margin is x114 (H2) or x398 (H1) in v² m_h², because eps scales as 1/(v² m_h²).

(1) The audit says the falloff is set by the pole. That is itself only true at leading order. At loop level the Higgs 2-point function has spectral support down to massless thresholds (via h→γγ and gg), so the far tail of the static profile is a power law, not e^{-m_h r}. The audit's 7e-11 width estimate covers only the complex pole. This adds to the tree-level narrowing of the range claim ('undetectable 54.7 attometres outside') rather than weakening it. Encoding caveats. These are recorded; none changes the grade.
(1) Part B's 'eps = -rho_H/(v^2 m_h^2)' is close to definitional. The script sets dphi = -J/m_h^2 and J = rho_H/v, then checks the substitution. (2) The domination-limit check is a toy of address.py section 9. It encodes r/d ~ m·sqrt(rho)/ln(rho) and leaves m_h out of the log argument. It passes for any m > 0 trivially. The conclusion that the theorem does not depend on m_h is right, but the check is weak.

A one-loop top estimate is not scheme-independent: the p^2-slope of the self-energy is UV-divergent and is absorbed by wavefunction renormalisation. (2) G_F. PDG 2024 Table 1.1 (ca6b3683…) reads '1.166 378 8(6)×10−5 GeV−2', 510 ppb. Eberhart eq.(21) reads 1.166 378 59(59)e-5, and its abstract confirms the O(α^3) QED and dispersive hadronic update over 'the previous prediction at order α^2'. I recomputed v as 246.219640 → 246.219662, so v^2 moves 1.80e-7, as claimed.

(3) v scheme. 1907.02500v5 gives v(Q0 = 173.1 GeV) = 246.60109 and λ = 0.12603842, and states 'at tree-level. Including radiative corrections'. That makes v^2 3.10e-3 higher, as claimed.

(4) m_e. The PDG 2026 sqlite (edition 2026) row S003M is 0.51099895069(16) MeV. address.py uses 0.51099895000 (CODATA 2018, which the PDG 2024 constants table also prints). (m_e/m_h)^2 moves 2.70e-9, under the claimed 3e-9.

(5) Γ_H. RPP 2026 gives 3.0 +1.5 −0.7 MeV. Re√(M²−iMΓ)/M − 1 = 7.19e-11, as claimed.

(6) κ_λ. 2503.11548 reads '−1.2 < κλ < +7.5' attributed to CMS PLB 861, 139210 (2025). Marking the CMS paper NAMED-NOT-READ is honest.

(7) Later literature. 2409.13663 has '125.04 ± 0.12 GeV' as 'the most precise single measurement'. 2308.04775 has 125.10 (Run 2) and 125.11 (combined). In 1307.3536v4 Table 3, λ goes from 0.12917 at LO to 0.12604 at NNLO, with M_h called the 'Pole mass'. The PDG 2024 EW review has 'v = 246.22 GeV', 'at tree level, i.e., to lowest order', M_H = λ v (10.5a), and 'There is no generally accepted convention to write the quartic term'. What is still missing is correctly called theory (the loop relation between pole mass and zero-momentum curvature) and is not computed, rather than presumed absent.

audits.name: Expansion scalar theta = nabla_mu u^mu = 3H for the comoving congruence in FLRW; zero for any volume-preserving flow; coordinate-invariant

source.located: Textbook identity (Raychaudhuri 1955 / Ehlers-Ellis 1+3 kinematics). Read at: G.F.R. Ellis & H. van Elst, 'Cosmological models (Cargese lectures 1998)', arXiv:gr-qc/9812046v5 (2 Sep 2008), sec.2.1.2 eq.(11), eq.(25), sec.4.1 eq.(104). Corroborating restatement: S. Kar & S. SenGupta, arXiv:gr-qc/0611123, eq.(10). The tree cites no source for this identity.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries page text for gr-qc/9812046v5 and gr-qc/0611123, returned in earlier stages of this workflow session and recovered verbatim from the session transcripts into scratchpad/d67/src/casmag/all/ (allpages.py; also src/gr-qc_9812046.harvest.txt). A fresh alphaXiv call this stage returned 'assistant quota exceeded', and the egress proxy refuses arxiv.org (403). So no new page was fetched this stage; the pages used are verbatim earlier tool output, not a paraphrase.

audits.published_statement: Ellis & van Elst eq.(11): 'nabla_a u_b = - u_a udot_b + (1/3) Theta h_ab + sigma_ab + omega_ab, where the trace Theta = tilde-nabla_a u^a is the rate of volume expansion scalar of the fluid (with H = Theta/3 the Hubble scalar)'. Eq.(25): 'Sdot/S = (1/3) Theta, so the volume of a fluid element varies as S^3.' Eq.(104), FLRW: 'Matter-comoving local coordinates can be found so that ds^2 = -dt^2 + S^2(t)(dr^2 + f^2(r) dOmega^2), u^a = delta^a_0 ... Sdot/S = (1/3) Theta, characterising S(t) as the scale factor for distances between any pair of fundamental observers.' Kar-SenGupta eq.(10): for u = d/dt in FLRW 'the shear and rotation are identically zero. The expansion is given as Theta = 3 adot/a'.
published_hypotheses: H1: u^a is a unit timelike vector field (eq.(4)), the 4-velocity of a chosen congruence. Theta is defined relative to that u^a ('of the fluid'; 'fundamental observers').
H2: Theta = 3H with H = Sdot/S requires FLRW geometry: perfect fluid with udot = sigma = omega = 0 everywhere (eq.(103)), and u^a the matter-comoving congruence u^a = delta^a_0 (eq.(104)).
H3: Theta is the fractional rate of change of a fluid element's volume along u (eq.(25)); Theta = 0 iff that volume is constant.
H4 (implicit): three spatial dimensions. The 1/3 in eq.(11) is 1/dim of the rest space (h^a_a = 3, eq.(5)).
H5 (application, not part of the identity): the real universe is FLRW only on large (homogeneity) scales. The lectures treat 'almost-FLRW' as an assumption to be justified.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED at obstruct.py:270-277 (row EXPANSION-IS-A-RELABELLING): 'the universe has theta = 3 H_0 ... theta is coordinate-invariant, so no relabelling moves it'. The row drops the congruence qualifier that permute.py:26 carries ('3H for a comoving congruence'), and the FLRW qualifier. Theta is a scalar of the pair (g,u), and rederive E shows this. The static Killing congruence of de Sitter (which is flat FLRW with a = e^{Ht}; pullback verified) has Theta = 0 exactly, at the same events where the comoving congruence has 3H. A tilted congruence in matter-FLRW has Theta != 3H. This does not refute 'no relabelling moves it': a diffeomorphism carries (g,u) with it, so Theta moves as a scalar (rederive C). What it does mean is that 'the universe has theta = 3H_0' is a claim about the fundamental-observer congruence, and choosing that congruence is a physical choice.

DROPPED at permute.py:26-33 and at the scorecard, permute.py:504-506 ('the expansion is a permutation: FALSIFIED'): the scale-of-validity hypothesis H5. The matter congruence has theta ~ 0 inside bound structures (sibling audit bound-systems-do-not-expand.json; arXiv:0911.0241, READ). So the falsification holds for the large-scale fundamental-observer flow, not for every sub-volume. The tree states it without qualification.

ADDED (the tree's own modelling, not from the source) at permute.py:200-202: a 'permutation of a closed index' is modelled as a measure-preserving flow, with theta hardcoded to 0.0. The external identity supplies only the conditional 'volume-preserving => theta = 0' (eq.(25)). That a Rubik-type rearrangement is such a flow is a declaration in the tree, not a computation. Recorded, not repaired.

Implicit at permute.py:196 ('Three, exactly -- one for each spatial direction'): correct only for isotropic expansion in 3 spatial dimensions (theta = nH; for anisotropic flows theta = H1+H2+H3). Not load-bearing.

permute.py:29 labels theta = 3H_0 'Measured, Planck 2018'. Planck's H_0 is a fit parameter of the LCDM-FLRW model (arXiv:1807.06209), so theta is inferred under H2/H5, not measured independently of them. Recorded as a status-word discrepancy.

rederivation.outcome: ALL CHECKS PASS (exit 0). A: nabla.u = 3 adot/a in FLRW for k = +1, 0, -1. B: the full 1+3 split from the Christoffels gives zero acceleration, zero shear, zero vorticity, and trace 3H. C: Theta is the same in conformal time, in proper-radius coordinates, and under a generic nonlinear (t,r) map with a = t^(2/3); relative error 0. A vacuity guard confirms that check can fail: the untransformed u gives 1.1007 against 1.0023. D: Theta = d ln sqrt(h)/dt, so Theta = 0 iff the flow preserves volume. E: the de Sitter static patch pulls back exactly to flat FLRW; its Killing congruence has Theta = 0 in both coordinate systems while the comoving congruence has 3H; a tilted congruence gives Theta - 3H = 0.19 at a test event. F: Theta = nH for n = 1..5. G: 3H0 = 6.549, 6.578, 6.661 and 7.101 e-18 /s.

later_literature.what: Theta = 3 adot/a for u = d/dt in FLRW, with shear and rotation identically zero. The text says 'a^6 is the volume' where the formula uses sqrt(a^6) = a^3. That is a wording discrepancy in the restatement (the formula is correct), not a refutation.

In LTB-Lambda models matched to FLRW, shells separating inner collapsing regions from outer expanding ones exist where theta + 3a vanishes, so the matter expansion is not 3H inside bound regions. This narrows the scope of 'the universe has theta = 3H'; the identity itself is untouched.

audits.lacked_data: The identity is kinematic: differential geometry of a chosen congruence on an FLRW metric, with no measured input. No missing datum can falsify it, and it was re-derived here for all three k and in four coordinate systems. What 1998-era authors lacked was the value of H0 (45-80 km/s/Mpc) and knowledge of the Hubble tension. Current values (67.36, 68.51, 73.04) move the printed theta by up to 8.4% but never toward zero, so the tree's conclusion that theta != 0 for the cosmic matter flow is unaffected. The evidence therefore runs against M's hypothesis for this result: no moved datum reaches the conclusion. Where 'incomplete' does apply, the gap is not in the authors' data but in the tree's scope. The identity holds for the fundamental-observer congruence of an exact FLRW metric, and the real matter flow has theta ~ 0 in bound structures (arXiv:0911.0241). One non-load-bearing discrepancy is recorded. The cached text of gr-qc/9812046v5 p.23 reads 'Hubble time 1/H0 of about 1.8 x 10^9' for H0 ~ 50, while 1/(50 km/s/Mpc) = 19.56 Gyr. This may be a superscript lost in extraction and must not be quoted as an error until the typeset PDF is read.
audits.grade_evidence: The external identity itself stands exactly. Ellis-van Elst eq.(11), (25) and (104) were re-derived in sympy: Theta = 3H for the comoving FLRW congruence for k = 0 and +-1, unchanged under every coordinate change tried (including a generic nonlinear one), and Theta = 0 iff the flow preserves volume. No moved datum takes theta to zero. The grade is NARROWED because the tree's use drops two hypotheses. (1) obstruct.py:270-277 drops 'comoving congruence'; rederive E exhibits a congruence in flat-FLRW de Sitter (the static Killing observers) with Theta = 0 exactly. (2) permute.py:26-33 and 504-506 assert 'the universe has theta = 3H_0' and 'THE UNIVERSE IS NOT A PERMUTATION' without the homogeneity-scale hypothesis, while the matter flow has theta ~ 0 in bound structures. Neither drop reverses the verdict for the large-scale fundamental-observer flow: no relabelling moves theta, and changing the congruence changes the observer family rather than relabelling it. The step 'permutation = measure-preserving flow' (hardcoded 0.0 at permute.py:200-202) is the tree's own declaration, not part of the external result.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the obstruct.py row names 'the comoving (fundamental-observer) congruence of FLRW'; permute.py names the homogeneity-scale hypothesis (theta = 3H for the cosmic-scale matter flow, ~0 inside bound structures); and the word 'Measured' becomes 'Planck-LCDM fit'. To WRONG: a computed coordinate transformation that changes the comoving congruence's nabla.u at a fixed event (none exists, since the divergence of a vector field is a scalar), or an FLRW solution whose comoving congruence has Theta != 3 adot/a. To DATA-DEPENDENT: only if the verdict rested on theta's numerical value rather than on theta != 0, and it does not.

verifiers.reason:
I re-read the source myself this stage with a fresh alphaXiv call on gr-qc/9812046v5 (pp.6-7, 9, 15, 21-22), and I reran the rederivation script. It passes every check (ALL CHECKS PASS). I agree with every computation in the audit. I do not agree with the grade, because NARROWED rests on reading two of the source's own conventions as hypotheses the tree dropped.

(1) The "congruence dropped" charge against obstruct.py:270-277. The source fixes u^a once, on p.6, as "the average motion of matter" through "fundamental observers", and says "We assume this 4-velocity is unique". It then writes Theta as the expansion "of the fluid" (eq.(11)). On p.22 it uses the same shorthand the tree uses: "because the Universe is expanding today (Theta_0 > 0)". That matches obstruct.py's "the universe has theta = 3 H_0" in form. Under the source's definitions, "the universe's Theta" already means the unique matter congruence, so the tree is not dropping a qualifier. The obstruct row also names the COMOVING frame itself at line 280. The audit's counterexamples fall outside the source's hypotheses:
- The de Sitter static Killing congruence is not a matter flow. Pure de Sitter has no fluid to fix u, which breaks the source's uniqueness premise.
- The tilted congruence is not the matter flow either.
- Changing the congruence is not a relabelling. The audit concedes this.

(2) The "scale hypothesis H5 dropped" charge against permute.py:26-33 and 504-506. The source defines u in a coarse-grained way: p.6 footnote 2, "a fluid description can be used on a large enough scale", and "average 4-velocity of matter in a suitably sized volume". The near-zero theta inside bound structures belongs to the fine-grained flow, which is not the source's u. Separately, the tree is falsifying a universal claim (a permutation has theta = 0 everywhere). One region with theta != 0 is enough to falsify it, so the verdict needs no restriction on where theta = 3H holds.

The audit itself says "Neither drop reverses the verdict", and its own route back to STANDS is a change of wording only. Grading NARROWED would therefore overstate things against the tree, which M's rules forbid in both directions.

These items are recorded but do not move the grade:
- permute.py:29 calls the value "Measured, Planck 2018", but Planck's H_0 is a LCDM fit. That is a status-word discrepancy. It does not narrow the result: SH0ES's low-z H_0 (73.04 +- 1.04) measures the local expansion of the matter flow almost directly and is also nonzero, at about 70 sigma. So theta != 0 does not depend on LCDM.
- The step "permutation = measure-preserving flow" (theta hardcoded to 0.0 at permute.py:200-202) is the tree's own modelling. It lies outside the external identity.

The external identity itself is READ, re-derived in sympy and coordinate-invariant, and no moved datum takes theta to zero. Proposed grade: STANDS, with the status-word note attached.

Not re-read: the p.23 "Hubble time 1.8 x 10^9" passage. It is not load-bearing and stays a discrepancy to check against the typeset PDF.

source.located: Primary classics, none on arXiv: Bennett, Brassard, Crepeau, Jozsa, Peres, Wootters, PRL 70, 1895 (1993) [teleportation]; Wootters & Zurek, Nature 299, 802 (1982) and Dieks, Phys. Lett. 92A, 271 (1982) [no-cloning]; Eberhard (1978) and Ghirardi-Rimini-Weber (1980) [no-communication]. Read live in this run at alphaXiv through exact restatements: (i) Pirandola, Eisert, Weedbrook, Furusawa, Braunstein, 'Advances in quantum teleportation', arXiv:1505.07831v1 (2015). Pages 1-2 give the protocol, the hypotheses, 'excludes superluminal communication', 'physical constituents of the original system remain at the sending location', the unknown-input clause with RSP, and F_class = 2/3. Pages 4-6 give experimental fidelities and distances. (ii) Scarani, Iblisdir, Gisin, Acin, 'Quantum cloning', RMP 77, 1225 (2005), arXiv:quant-ph/0511088v1. Pages 2-4 give the theorem, the proof 'using only the linearity', and Herbert FLASH. Page 6 gives the no-signalling bound eta <= 2/3 (F <= 5/6) and the converse that no linear TP-CP map signals. Page 30 on teleportation: 'the original has to be destroyed ...'. (iii) Peres & Terno, 'Quantum information and relativity theory', RMP 76, 93 (2004), arXiv:quant-ph/0212023v2. Pages 8-10 give the no-communication theorem (eqs. 9-11), the assumption 'we assume that there are no closed causal loops', and the teleportation identity (eq. 19). source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1505.07831, quant-ph/0511088 and quant-ph/0212023. The page text came back verbatim in this run and every quotation is taken from it. Bennett 1993, Wootters-Zurek 1982, Dieks 1982, Eberhard 1978 and GRW 1980 are NAMED-NOT-READ in themselves: each is attributed only through the three restatements, which cite them by reference number. audits.published_statement: Teleportation (1505.07831 p.1): 'an unknown quantum state of a physical system is measured and subsequently reconstructed or reassembled at a remote location (the physical constituents of the original system remain at the sending location). This process requires classical communication and excludes superluminal communication. Most importantly, it requires the resource of quantum entanglement.' From p.2: Alice's Bell detection projects a and A onto (P_k (x) I)|Phi>. 'The state of Alice's input qubit has been collapsed by measurement while Bob's qubit B is simultaneously projected onto P_k^+ rho P_k.' Alice sends k and Bob applies P_k, which gives 'an exact replica of Alice's input state in the ideal case (F = 1)'. Also p.2: 'Alice's input state is assumed to be unknown, otherwise the protocol reduces to remote state preparation.' No-cloning (quant-ph/0511088 p.3): 'No quantum operation exists that can duplicate perfectly an arbitrary quantum state', proved 'using only the linearity of quantum transformations'. From p.30: in teleportation 'the original has to be destroyed in the process and the Bell-state measurement should not provide any information of the state to be teleported, otherwise there would be a contradiction with the no-cloning theorem (more precisely, with the optimal asymmetric cloning result)'. No-communication (quant-ph/0212023 pp.8-9): if [A_mu m, B_nu n] = 0 then p_nu = tr(sum_n B_nu n rho B_nu n^+). 'The statistics of Bob's result are not affected at all by what Alice may simultaneously do somewhere else', with the stated assumption 'there are no closed causal loops'.
published_hypotheses: Q1: the input state is UNKNOWN to Alice; otherwise the protocol is remote state preparation (1505.07831 p.2).

Q2: the parties share a pure entangled resource, maximally entangled 'in the ideal case' (a Bell pair). Fidelity F = 1 holds only in the ideal case; with decoherence F lies in [0,1] (1505.07831 pp.1-2).
Q3: Alice makes a complete Bell detection on a and A. The outcome k (2 bits for a qubit, d^2 signals in dimension d) goes over a classical channel, and Bob applies U_k (1505.07831 p.2).
Q4: quantum dynamics is linear, i.e. a trace-preserving completely positive map. No-cloning is 'a consequence of the linearity of quantum mechanics' (quant-ph/0511088 pp.3-4).
Q5: the two parties' local operations commute ([A, B] = 0). What cannot change is Bob's non-selective, outcome-averaged statistics (quant-ph/0212023 eqs. 9-11).
Q6: there are no closed causal loops (chronology is respected), classical signals are bounded by c, and the Lorentz group is implemented unitarily (quant-ph/0212023 p.9 and p.13).
Q7: the physical constituents of the input stay with the sender. Bob's system is already in place and may be of a different kind, e.g. light to matter (1505.07831 p.1, p.6).
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED Q2 (F = 1) where R11 binds MOVE and CONSUMED. specthm.py:1188-1189 records 'the specification is a quantum state; the fidelity is not yet fixed'. Yet specthm.py:1205-1213 and ledger.py:1413-1418 bind IT_IS_A_MOVE_NOT_A_COPY and CHANNEL_IS_CONSUMED_BY_USE, and the source gives both exactly only at F = 1. Computed (rederive H): a measure-prepare channel reaches F = 2/3 with zero ebits spent, so the channel is not consumed. Clone-then-teleport leaves A a 5/6 copy while B gets 5/6, so it is not a pure move. Scarani p.30 ties 'move' to the optimal ASYMMETRIC cloning trade-off: it is graded in F, not a yes/no flag.

DROPPED Q4+Q6 (linear, chronology-respecting quantum mechanics). Neither is named anywhere in transit.py, in the specthm.py R11 hypotheses (:1187-1191) or in ledger.py M-S1A-P5 (:1410-1427). Yet the same R11 row lists O3 as open (specthm.py:1201-1203: 'whether any braneworld shortcut yields a CTC is O3'). Read at source: Ahn-Myers-Ralph-Mann (1207.6062 pp.1-4) clone arbitrary qubits above the 5/6 bound using a Deutsch CTC, without signalling. Bielinska-Eckstein-Horodecki (2412.20854) find that generic nonlinear dynamics allows statistical superluminal signalling. Computed (rederive H): a perfect nonlinear cloner at Bob turns Alice's two ensembles, both I/2, into states that differ (<01|rho|01> = 1/4 vs 0).

WEAKENED Q5 (non-selective) in the wording. transit.py:17-19 and :279 say B's state is invariant 'under EVERY operation A can perform'. The source theorem covers Bob's outcome-averaged statistics. Computed (rederive NS): the identity holds for a generic symbolic Kraus operator and a generic 4x4 rho, but the state conditioned on Alice's outcome does move (|0><0| vs I/2). transit.py also tests only unitaries (:106-110, :173, :316). The theorem covers every trace-preserving map, so the claim is true even though the tested class is narrower.

ADDED a traversal clause the source does not contain: specthm.py:1193 says 'The channel must be traversed at <= c to exist'. transit.py:46-49 and :251-254 say 'A Bell pair spanning distance D required something to cross D at <= c beforehand ... THE CORRIDOR MUST BE TRAVERSED IN ORDER TO EXIST'. The source needs a SHARED pair, not a pair that was carried. Computed (rederive V): local operations alone, SWAP_{A,m1} (x) SWAP_{m2,B} on a medium that is already entangled, give A and B a full Bell pair. Read at source (Reznik quant-ph/0212044 p.1, pp.7-12): probes that are causally disconnected become entangled from the vacuum. Checked for over-representation the other way: in Reznik's inertial model the entanglement survives only for L/T < 1.1, so the switching time is about the light time anyway. The entanglement is weak, vanishes with separation, and becomes a usable pair only after LOCC purification, which needs classical communication at <= c (Reznik p.13). So the mechanism clause is narrowed, the setup time (specthm.py:1196, 4.2465 yr at Proxima) is not shown wrong, and BEATS_LIGHT is untouched.

RETAINED Q1: H_tele (specthm.py:1190-1191; ledger.py:1426-1427) and the KNOWN-state clause (specthm.py:1214-1215) match 1505.07831 p.2, 'otherwise the protocol reduces to remote state preparation'. No drift.

RETAINED Q7 for CARRIES_SUBSTANCE = False (1505.07831 p.1). transit.py also says 'It moves no mass and no energy' (:57, :261). R11 and M-S1A-P5 do not use that sentence, so it is not graded here; it is audited under the sibling key teleportation-transfers-state-not-matter.

INSTRUMENT DISCREPANCIES in the tree's code, not the external result (recorded, not repaired). Three values are declared rather than computed: CHANNEL_BITS_AFTER = 0.0 is a constant (transit.py:139); A's 'S = 1 bit' is the entropy of a hard-coded I/2 (:230, :341-342); advantage_over_light is D/c - D/c by definition (:145-146). All three come out TRUE when computed (rederive C, M, L). 'NO WORLDLINE CROSSES ANYTHING' (:21-22, :192-193) conflicts with the file's own 2 classical bits and its prior pair distribution (:37-50). 'CONSERVATION LAW' (:24, :213, :221, :283) actually describes LOCC monotonicity: entanglement is not conserved, since local operations can destroy it, but LOCC cannot increase it.

MOVE: Alice's pair ends in Bell state k and her input qubit in I/2, with no dependence on t or f. NO-CLONING: a linear cloner of {0,1} sends |+> to a Bell state (overlap^2 = 1/2), and <x|y> = <x|y>^2 has only the solutions 0 and 1. CONSUMED: Bob's qubit is pure on every outcome, so the entanglement between Alice's lab and B goes from 1 to 0; teleporting half of a Bell pair yields a full R|B ebit, which is the LOCC-monotonicity argument. NO-SIGNALLING: Tr_A[(K(x)I)rho(K(x)I)^+] = Tr_A[(K^+K(x)I)rho] holds for a generic symbolic K and rho, so no trace-preserving Alice map changes rho_B; the state conditioned on Alice's outcome does move. BITS WITHHELD: rho_B = I/2 identically. LIGHT: arrival - D/c = t_BSM >= 0, and transit.py's advantage is 0 by definition. Hypothesis tests: measure-prepare gives F = 2/3 with no ebit spent; clone-then-teleport keeps 5/6 at A; a nonlinear perfect cloner signals (1/4 vs 0); local SWAPs on a pre-entangled medium make a Bell pair with nothing traversing; 1/768.0665 mas = 4.2465 ly.

later_literature.what: With a Deutsch CTC (a nonlinear fixed-point map), an arbitrary qubit is cloned above the 5/6 bound using finite resources, and this does NOT signal. No-cloning therefore needs chronology to be respected; no-signalling survives in their construction.

Revisits Gisin / Simon-Buzek-Gisin: no-signalling plus the static structure of quantum mechanics force linear CPTP dynamics. Generic nonlocal nonlinear dynamics permits statistical superluminal signalling in all three protocols studied; no-signalling survives only if the measurable observables are radically restricted. This confirms linearity (Q4) as the hypothesis BEATS_LIGHT = False rests on.

Probes that are causally disconnected end up entangled from the vacuum. For inertial probes this needs L/T < 1.1, so the switching time is about the light time. The entanglement is weak, vanishes with separation, and becomes usable only after LOCC purification, which needs classical communication. This narrows the tree's added traversal clause; it does not touch BEATS_LIGHT or the setup time.

In conical spacetimes, which include (d+1)-Minkowski for d > 1, no-superluminal-signalling rules out every operationally detectable causal loop; in 1+1 dimensions it does not. This bears on the board's open O3 row, not directly on the teleportation flags.
Titles and abstracts only. All of them probe the same two hypotheses, linearity and chronology; none claims signalling or cloning within linear, chronology-respecting quantum mechanics.

audits.lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested for this result. The 1978-82 authors (Eberhard, GRW, Wootters-Zurek, Dieks) and Bennett et al. (1993) had the formalism of linear quantum mechanics and no teleportation experiment; the first experiments came in 1997-98. What came later: teleportation in photons, atoms, ions, NMR and solid state, at 80-89% fidelity over 16-143 km, always with active classical feed-forward (1505.07831 pp.4-6). These results are theorems about the formalism, so the only data that could move them would be data refuting linearity (Q4) or chronology (Q6). Evidence either way: nothing read here reports signalling, cloning above 5/6, or teleportation without the classical channel. The later work that does bite is conditional theory, not data: CTC cloning (1207.6062) and nonlinear signalling (2412.20854) show what follows IF those hypotheses fail, and nothing read here says they fail. So missing data does not change the result. What the tree lacks is not data but three named hypotheses: F = 1, linear chronology-respecting quantum mechanics, and the difference between a shared pair and a carried one.
audits.grade_evidence: The external results stand as published, and all of them are re-derived exactly here (22/22, sympy): the move, no-cloning, 1 -> 0 ebit on every outcome, no change to rho_B under any trace-preserving Alice map, I/2 without the bits, and arrival >= D/c. H_tele (the unknown-state hypothesis) is retained. The grade is NARROWED under the rule 'a hypothesis the tree drops', on three counts. (1) F = 1: R11 leaves the fidelity unfixed (specthm.py:1189) but still binds MOVE and CONSUMED, and those fail at F <= 2/3 (no ebit spent) and are only partial below F = 1 (a 5/6 copy survives). (2) Linear, chronology-respecting quantum mechanics is never named, although the same R11 row keeps O3 (CTCs) open; read at source, Deutsch-CTC cloning beats 5/6 (1207.6062) and nonlinear dynamics generically signals (2412.20854). (3) The tree ADDS 'the channel must be traversed to exist' (specthm.py:1193; transit.py:46-49), where the source needs only a shared pair. Local operations on a pre-entangled medium make such a pair (computed), and vacuum entanglement exists across causally disconnected regions (Reznik, READ). In Reznik's inertial model, though, the switching time is about the light time and purification needs classical communication, so the setup-time figure is not shown wrong. Over-representation checked both ways: in the scenario the tree actually runs (F = 1, unknown state, linear quantum mechanics, no CTC) all four flags hold, so nothing is WRONG. The declared constants and the zero advantage that holds by definition are discrepancies in how the tree presents the result, and each computes true here. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: the one datum, Proxima at 4.2465 ly, enters no flag.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names F = 1 (or restates MOVE and CONSUMED as graded in F), names linear chronology-respecting quantum mechanics as a hypothesis of all four flags (tying them to O3 staying closed), and restates the traversal clause as 'a usable pair needs carriage or LOCC distillation, each at <= c'. To WRONG: an experiment showing signalling through entanglement alone, cloning above 5/6 where chronology is respected, or teleportation of an unknown state without a classical channel. Nothing read here reports any of these. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a measured violation of quantum linearity, or a realised CTC. To OPEN: none applies; the restatements were read live and the claims are finite and machine-checked.

- quant-ph/0511088 p.3 has the proof "using only the linearity", p.6 the bound eta <= 2/3 (F <= 5/6) and the statement that no linear TP-CP map signals, and p.30 has teleportation: "the original has to be destroyed ... BSM should not provide any information ... (more precisely, with the optimal asymmetric cloning result)".
- 1207.6062 pp.1-4 shows that Deutsch-CTC cloning beats the bound and "does not violate no-signalling criteria". The auditor did not say two things here. The bound is beaten only numerically, for N >= 55, under root fidelity sqrt(5/6). And the paper itself notes the contrary view of Bennett et al. 2009 (ref 13), so the narrowing comes from a disputed model, not a settled one.
- Every quotation the audit uses checks out against the page text.

COUNT (2) STANDS, AND IT ALONE CARRIES NARROWED
- latticectc.py:108-109 has O3_STATUS 'OPEN (narrowed) -- NOT CLOSED' and O3_CLOSED = False.
- latticectc is an owner of the same R11 row (specthm.py:1186). The R11 statement keeps the CTC question open at :1201-1203.
- Yet neither transit.py, the R11 hypotheses (:1187-1191) nor ledger.py M-S1A-P5 (:1410-1427) names chronology or linearity, which is the source's own stated assumption. That is a hypothesis the tree drops, so NARROWED under the rule.

COUNT (3) STANDS, AS A NARROWING OF THE TREE'S ADDED CLAUSE
- The clause is 'the channel must be traversed at <= c to exist' (specthm.py:1193; transit.py:46-49).
- One weakness: the auditor's SWAP construction begs the question, because the medium is already entangled across D.
- The finding is carried instead by Reznik's vacuum entanglement. The auditor correctly limits this to the mechanism clause: it leaves the setup time and BEATS_LIGHT untouched.

COUNT (1) IS PARTLY A MISREADING. Computed in verify/refute/tele_nonideal.py (sympy, exact).
- Under H_tele, meaning teleportation actually performed with a complete Bell measurement on (a,A), the state after the measurement is (aA) (x) B, a product, on all four outcomes. This holds for a pure non-maximal resource cos(al)|00>+sin(al)|11> and for a Werner resource of any p.
- So CHANNEL_IS_CONSUMED_BY_USE holds whatever the resource fidelity. It does not need F = 1.
- The counterexample 'measure-prepare reaches 2/3 with zero ebits spent' is not teleportation, so it falls outside H_tele. The same is true of 'clone-then-teleport': there Alice teleports a clone, not the input.
- MOVE is resource-dependent, but narrower than the audit says. With the Werner resource the outcomes stay at p_k = 1/4, so the move is exact even though Bob's F < 1. With a non-maximal pure resource, p_k = 1/4 ± [cos(2al-t)+cos(2al+t)]/8 depends on the input state. Alice's classical record then leaks information, which is Scarani p.30's caveat.
- So the dropped hypothesis is 'a maximally entangled resource, or a Bell measurement with outcomes independent of the input', binding MOVE only. It is not 'F = 1' binding both MOVE and CONSUMED.
- The audit also reads 'the fidelity is not yet fixed' (specthm.py:1189) as teleportation fidelity. In context it is M-S1A-P5's question about the specification ('what is specified, at what fidelity'). That reading is contestable.

CHECKED IN THE OTHER DIRECTION (TOWARD WRONG OR STANDS)
- In the scenario the tree actually runs, all four flags hold: transit.py --selftest PASS, and the rederive script gives 22/0.
- Nothing read reports signalling, cloning above 5/6, or teleportation without the classical channel. Not WRONG.
- The one datum, D, enters no flag. Not DATA-DEPENDENT.

The grade stays NARROWED. Count (1) should be restated: CONSUMED holds for any resource under H_tele, and only MOVE needs a maximally entangled resource (more precisely, Bell-measurement outcomes independent of the input). The Ahn et al. CTC narrowing should be marked as resting on the Deutsch model, which is disputed.

verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION (encoding check plus vacuity guard)
verifiers.reason:
RE-RUN: I copied the audit's script to verify/rederive/tele_nocloning/tele.py and ran it. Result: 22 passed, 0 failed, exit 0, the same as the audit reports. transit.py --selftest passes. The tree lines the audit cites match HEAD dbb3c9c: specthm.py:1185-1216 says 'the fidelity is not yet fixed', 'The channel must be traversed at <= c to exist', H_tele and the KNOWN-state clause; ledger.py:1410-1427 is M-S1A-P5; transit.py:139 and :145-146 show CHANNEL_BITS_AFTER = 0.0 and advantage = D/c - D/c.

ENCODING. The core checks test the theorem itself, symbolically, not a toy:
- P/M/B use a symbolic psi(t, f).
- NS proves Tr_A[(K(x)I)rho(K(x)I)^+] = Tr_A[(K^+K(x)I)rho] for a generic complex K and a generic, non-Hermitian 4x4 rho. That identity is Peres-Terno eqs. 9-11 in the qubit case, and the algebra is the same in any dimension.

But about 6 of the 22 'passes' are declared, not computed. That is the same fault the audit charges the tree with:
- 'outcome statistics carry nothing' is chk(True). The p_k = 1/4 behind it was computed in P, so this one is a restatement.
- 'hence ANY trace-preserving map' is chk(True).
- 'clone(5/6)-then-teleport keeps 5/6 at A' only tests 5/6 > 2/3. No cloner is run.
- 'optimal cloner F = 5/6' is (1 + eta)/2 with eta = 2/3 put in by hand.
- 'no flag depends on D' is chk(True).
- The L checks are true by construction, which the script itself admits.

I computed the missing ones myself:
- The Buzek-Hillery cloner gives F1 = F2 = 5/6 exactly.
- A summed two-Kraus amplitude-damping channel on Alice leaves rho_B unchanged for a generic rho, with zero difference.

The conclusions stand. The '22 computed' count overstates.

VACUITY GUARD (tele_vacuity.py, vac2.py). Negating each hypothesis breaks the checks that should break:
- Product resource |00> (Q2 negated): F = cos^2(t/2) and sin^2(t/2), not 1.
- No Pauli corrections (Q3 negated): F is not 1.
- A non-trace-preserving Alice operation diag(1,0) changes rho_B to [[1/2,0],[0,0]].
- A non-commuting joint CNOT (Q5 negated) moves rho_B.
- A nonlinear perfect cloner signals (already in the script: 1/4 vs 0).
- Measure-prepare re-integrated gives 2/3.

Two checks are NOT discriminating on their own:
- (a) The M check that Alice's side is psi-free (her pair ends in Bell state k, her input qubit in I/2) still passes with a product resource. So 'move' rests entirely on P's F = 1, and M alone shows nothing about the resource.
- (b) C's 'Bob is pure after' still passes with a product resource. Only the 'before = 1 ebit' check gives it content.

The V check presupposes what it claims to show. With the medium unentangled, the same local SWAPs give F(Phi+) = 1/2. V only shows that a pair which ALREADY spans D needs no further traversal; it says nothing about how that pair arose. So V cannot carry count (3).

Count (3) rests only on Reznik (vacuum entanglement), which I did not re-read. By the audit's own account, Reznik's entanglement becomes usable only after LOCC distillation, which needs classical communication across D at <= c. So the tree's substantive claim, that something must cross D at <= c before a usable channel exists, is not refuted; only 'carried' versus 'communicated' is narrowed. Count (3) is therefore a wording-level narrowing, weaker than the grade_evidence presents it.

Counts (1) and (2) survive the re-run:
- (1) F = 1 is load-bearing. The BH cloner and measure-prepare computations confirm that MOVE and CONSUMED are graded in F.
- (2) Linearity is load-bearing (the nonlinear cloner signals). The non-TP and non-commuting tests also show trace-preservation and commuting local operations are load-bearing. Chronology was not machine-checked here; it rests on the reading of 1207.6062.

GRADE: NARROWED is supported. Nothing computed here makes a flag WRONG under F = 1, an unknown state, linear trace-preserving commuting quantum mechanics and no CTC. I am not refuting the audit. The corrections to carry into the record:
- (i) The '22 passed' count includes about 6 declared or tautological checks. Two of them are now computed above.
- (ii) The V check is vacuous as evidence against the traversal clause.
- (iii) Count (3) should read 'mechanism wording narrowed', not 'clause added and shown false'.

verifiers.reason:
Every data row holds where it matters. None of the defects found changes moves_conclusion, and none changes the grade. They are wording and attribution slips, recorded here and not repaired.

(1) Proxima distance. 1000/768.0665 mas = 1.3019706 pc = 4.246460 ly, which rounds to 4.2465. The ±0.0499 mas uncertainty gives 4.24618 to 4.24674 ly. The figure enters no flag, so 'moves_conclusion: No' follows. One slip: the row and rederive line 245 say the parallax is used 'as the tree cites it' / 'as the tree's foliation.py cites'. The tree has only 4.2465 and the label 'Gaia DR3 parallax' (foliation.py:583, nonstatic.py:257, ledger.py:333). The value 768.0665 is not anywhere in the tree; it comes from docket67-raw/run1-partial-fable/rederive/codata-2018-constants.py:48. The audit itself admits the parallax was not re-read at source, which is honest, so this is a misattribution and not a fabrication.

(2) F_class = 2/3. Confirmed verbatim, 1505.07831 p.2. The value_then attribution (Massar-Popescu 1995) comes after Bennett 1993, but it is dated, so nothing is hidden.

(3) 5/6. Confirmed: quant-ph/0511088 p.4 (Buzek-Hillery 1996, eq. 4), p.6 (eta <= 2/3) and p.8 (eq. 14).

(4) Experiments. Confirmed in 1505.07831:
- 16 km at 89% with real-time feed-forward (p.4);
- about 100 km at 80% or better (p.5);
- 143 km at 83% or better with active feed-forward (p.5);
- the first experiments in 1997-98 (refs 16, 18, 28, 29).
The CV value of about 83% is in Table I on p.10, not pp.4-6, so that page citation is wrong.

A factual overstatement: lacked_data says 'always with active classical feed-forward (pp.4-6)' and the row says 'every experiment uses classical feed-forward'. Page 4 contradicts this: 'In other experiments the feed-forward is instead simulated in the post-processing'. The photonic-chip 89% was 'extrapolated ... by simulating the feed-forward' (p.5), and Innsbruck was post-selected, called 'a posteriori teleportation' (p.4). Each of these experiments still needs the classical Bell outcome, so the conclusion and BEATS_LIGHT do not move, but the sentence should read 'always uses the classical Bell outcome, in real time or in post-processing'.

(5) Was M's hypothesis answered with evidence, not presumed? Mostly yes. The audit names what the 1978-93 authors lacked (any experiment) and what came later (cross-platform experiments at 80-89%, all needing the classical channel). It correctly says these are theorems of the formalism, which only data against linearity (Q4) or chronology (Q6) could move. It keeps conditional theory (1207.6062, 2412.20854) separate from data. One gap: evidence for Q4 also exists, namely the experimental bounds on nonlinear quantum mechanics from the Weinberg-type tests (e.g. Bollinger et al. 1989). The audit cites none of it, so its 'evidence either way' is one-sided by omission. That bounds is NAMED-NOT-READ here; it would strengthen the result, not weaken it.

The rederivation was rerun: 22 passed, 0 failed, including the Proxima check and the D-independence of every flag. The grade stays NARROWED on the audit's hypothesis-drift grounds, which this lens does not touch. It is not DATA-DEPENDENT, because no datum enters any flag.
